cards.title: Gi Signaling Does Not Differentiate Hallucinogenic from Nonhallucinogenic 5-HT2A Receptor Agonists.
cards.post: A recent publication by Xu et al. suggests that Gi activation following 5-HT2AR stimulation differentiates hallucinogenic from nonhallucinogenic agonists. Here, we reanalyze the author's source data to demonstrate that Gi activation is less predictive of hallucinogenic potential than canonical effectors of 5-HT2AR signaling.

cards.title: The molecular and neurochemical basis of altered intrinsic neural timescales in major depressive disorder: a multimodal imaging-transcriptomic investigation of esketamine and sertraline treatment.
cards.post: Background: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by dysfunction in higher-order cortical regions involved in emotional and cognitive processes; however, its neurobiological basis remains unclear. Methods: A total of 57 healthy controls and 41 patients with MDD were included. Results: Compared with healthy controls, patients with MDD exhibited significantly elevated INT levels in the left and right precuneus. Following treatment, patients with MDD showed significantly increased INT in the left occipital midline region and left calcarine cortex. Conclusion: These findings support a multiscale pathophysiological framework involving brain connectivity dynamics, molecular architecture, and neurochemical regulation in MDD.

cards.title: Working memory neural correlates after ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized placebo-controlled functional magnetic resonance imaging study.
cards.post: Aim: This secondary analysis investigated behavioral and neural changes during a working memory task post-ketamine infusion in TRD participants versus healthy volunteers (HVs). Methods: Data were previously collected from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial of 22 unmedicated TRD participants (14F/8 M) and 19 matched HVs (12F/7 M). Participants received ketamine (0.5mg/kg) and placebo two weeks apart. Results: Ketamine significantly reduced Montgomery-Asberg Depression Rating Scale scores compared to placebo (p < 0.01). In region of interest (ROI) analyses, TRD participants showed reduced activation in the superior temporal gyrus versus HVs (p < 0.01) after both infusions, and both groups demonstrated decreased parieto-occipital junction activation post-ketamine versus post-placebo (p = 0.01). Conclusion: Ketamine's antidepressant effects occurred without significant changes in working memory performance, though region-specific task-related brain changes were observed.

cards.post: Aim: In this study, two of these apps were validated against in-house software. Methods: Data were acquired in-house from 14 subjects who received placebo in a randomized controlled clinical trial and underwent two PET measurements using the radioligand [ 11 C]UCB-J. cards.title: A General-Purpose Adaptable Foundation Model for Total-Body PET Kinetic Modelling.
cards.post: Background: Voxel-level kinetic modeling in total-body dynamic positron emission tomography (TB-PET) enables precise physiological quantification but complicates parameter uncertainty estimation. Methods: To address this, we introduce LoRACM, a parameter-efficient framework utilizing low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to transfer a pretrained foundation CM to novel TB-PET scenarios. Results: In human data, LoRACM generated total-body K_i maps comparable to the ones made by non-negative nonlinear least squares (NNLS) fitting and a consistency model trained from scratch. Striatal dopamine binding potential estimates predicted by LoRACM correlated with NNLS estimates (r = 0.968-0.988). Conclusion: These underscore the potential of adapting a pretrained CM with LoRA for fast and reliable posterior parameter inference for kinetic models across distinct TB-PET applications.

cards.title: Multi-receptor whole-brain modeling reveals affinity-driven chemoarchitectural mechanism of virtual atomoxetine action
cards.post: Aim: Here, we combined pharmacological resting-state fMRI with a whole-brain model incorporating cortical expression of adrenergic and dopaminergic receptors to investigate the effects of atomoxetine, a norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor that globally elevates catecholaminergic … Methods: Using receptor similarity, we first identified a catecholaminergic chemoarchitecture comprising frontal, posterior and temporal networks, providing the neurochemical scaffold for interpreting atomoxetine-induced brain dynamics. Results: Whole-brain modeling revealed that although individual receptor parameters did not differ between conditions, their collective organization converged toward empirical receptor binding affinities. In silico forward modeling showed that this affinity-driven redistribution gave rise to a cortical modulation pattern aligned with a frontal chemoarchitectural gradient, which was sufficient to simulate the observed dynamical and connectivity changes. Conclusion: Together, these findings suggest receptor binding affinity as a key organizing principle linking molecular receptor organization to brain dynamics, providing a model-based, biologically interpretable computational mechanism through which global catecholaminergic perturbations reshape whole-brain function.

cards.title: Disruptions in brain hierarchical organisation reveal Alzheimer's disease progression
cards.post: Background: However, it remains unclear whether disease progression alters the causal hierarchical organisation of large-scale brain dynamics. Methods: We examined hierarchical brain organisation across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum using multimodal neuroimaging from 134 participants in the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (46 amyloid-negative cognitively normal, 36 amyloid-positive cognitively normal, 31 amyloid-positive mild cognitive … Results: Amyloid-negative cognitively normal exhibited a well-stratified hierarchy in which somatomotor and frontoparietal regions acted as sources, the default mode network occupied an intermediate integrative position, and memory, limbic, and visual systems acted as sinks. Conclusion: These findings suggest that Alzheimer’s pathology selectively disrupts hierarchical brain organisation.

cards.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of EEG biomarkers for Parkinson's disease: robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability across multiple datasets.
cards.post: Background: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a high-temporal-resolution, noninvasive window into some of the abnormalities underlying Parkinson's disease (PD), yet reported electrophysiological biomarkers vary widely across studies due to differences in preprocessing, feature extraction … Methods: Here we provide the first comprehensive, multi-dataset benchmarking of 16 EEG-derived biomarkers, including phase-amplitude coupling, beta burst metrics, aperiodic components, complexity measures, and beta waveform features, to evaluate their robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability. Results: In contrast, oscillatory biomarkers, including beta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, burst-derived metrics, and waveform-asymmetry features, showed substantial variability across methodological choices and lower within-session consistency. Fully-denoised data improved group-level separability, for several biomarkers in Dataset 1. Conclusion: Together, these findings identify several biomarkers with comparatively strong methodological robustness for further biological and clinical validation and highlight methodological factors that contribute to inconsistencies in the PD literature.

Conclusion

Together, these findings identify several biomarkers with comparatively strong methodological robustness for further biological and clinical validation and highlight methodological factors that contribute to inconsistencies in the PD literature.

cards.title: Cortical-fluidic dimensional mapping isolates GRIN2A-driven dysconnectivity and pharmacological network degradation in schizophrenia.
cards.post: Background: Standard connectivity models fail to capture the transient spatial kinematics underlying schizophrenia pathophysiology. Methods: The algorithm processed over 7000 memory testing sessions from 364 healthy participants. The validation phase evaluated a pre-existing clinical repository comprising 300 de-identified psychiatric records. Results: Cuneus dysconnectivity links strictly to global symptom severity. The methodology establishes an objective biomarker. Conclusion: The system links molecular glutamatergic vulnerabilities to macroscopic neural degradation in treatment-resistant psychiatric conditions.

cards.title: Directional brain-heart interaction during cognitive workload: a permutation conditional mutual information approach
cards.post: Aim: In this study, we investigated the use of Permutation Conditional Mutual Information (PCMI) for the characterization of directional BHI. Methods: First, the method was evaluated on synthetically generated coupled time series to assess its ability to detect the dominant direction of interaction. Results: The results show that BHI complexity increases during mental arithmetic tasks compared with baseline, supporting the role of cognitive workload in modulating brain–heart dynamics. These changes primarily involved anterior and posterior scalp regions, and affected both vagal- and sympathovagal-related HRV components. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate that PCMI provides a framework for studying directional BHI during cognitive tasks, and highlight its potential translational value for investigating broader brain–body interactions.

cards.title: Brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression: Desynchronization between salience network neuropsychological connectivity and heart rate variability.
cards.post: Background: However, the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms of body brain communication remain unclear. Methods: 293 depressed patients (145 with somatic symptoms and 148 without), and 160 healthy controls underwent magnetoencephalography during a resting state. Results: Individuals with somatic depression exhibited lower HRV, accompanied by theta hyper-connectivity within the salience network. Although higher theta connectivity was linked to increased HRV in controls, this correlation was attenuated or even reversed in patients with somatic depression. Conclusion: Our findings identify a specific pattern of brain-heart decoupling in somatic depression, characterized by disrupted communication between salience network theta oscillations and autonomic cardiac regulation.

cards.title: Temporal imprecision of the self in drug-free psychosis: Abnormal infraslow phase dynamics and brain complexity
cards.post: Background: Self-disturbance is a core feature of schizophrenia (SCZ) and may emerge during the prodromal phase. Methods: Temporal imprecision has recently been proposed as a core neural mechanism in schizophrenia, primarily demonstrated in faster EEG frequency ranges. Results: Compared to controls, EP drug-free showed higher SampEn and slower mean PF with greater variability than HC, particularly in the regions of the exteroceptive self. Both SampEn and PF significantly contributed to diagnostic classification, and increased SampEn was associated with greater severity of negative, disorganized, and anxiety/depression symptoms. Conclusion: Together, these findings indicate abnormal infraslow brain dynamics in early psychosis, characterized by increased neural complexity and disrupted temporal organization.

cards.title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
cards.post: Background: Although the role of the brain-gut axis in sleep regulation is increasingly recognized, the dynamic information flow and its directionality among the brain, heart, and gut systems during sleep remain unclear … Methods: In this study, based on overnight sleep data from 24 healthy subjects, we simultaneously collected occipital electroencephalogram (EEG), electrocardiogram, and bowel sound signals, constructed a multimodal physiological signal analysis framework, and employed a multivariate … Results: Sleep-stage dynamics further dissociate within-system from inter-system information flow: internal information exchange within the brain and gut intensifies with sleep depth and weakens during REM, whereas inter-system pathways show divergent stage-dependent patterns: heart-to-brain flow increases from light to deep sleep, while heart-to-gut and brain-to-gut flow are suppressed during deep sleep. Conclusion: This study identifies exploratory statistical patterns of directional information flow among the brain, heart, and gut systems during sleep, providing hypothesis-generating observations for future studies on sleep and multi-organ interactions.

cards.title: Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload: A Unified Theoretical Framework Linking DMT and Ketamine Through Sigma-1 Convergence, Entropic Saturation, and Workspace Flooding
cards.post: Background: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing. Methods: Here, we propose a novel unified framework for “Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload,” arguing that DMT and ketamine achieve unresponsiveness not by silencing neural activity but by saturating cortical information processing beyond the capacity … Results: The Dissociative Overload model reframes general anesthesia as a family of states unified by the failure to model external reality, achievable through either information deprivation or information saturation. Conclusion: While the framework is empirically grounded for ketamine, its extension to DMT-induced anesthesia constitutes a central prediction awaiting direct experimental validation.

cards.title: A multi-institutional investigation of psilocybin's effects on mouse behavior.
cards.post: Aim: Here, we implemented a multi-institutional collaborative approach to define the robust and replicable effects of the psychedelic drug psilocybin on mouse behavior. Results: Through this coordinated approach, we found that psilocybin had several robust and replicable acute effects on mouse behavior, including increased anxiety- and avoidance-related behaviors and decreased fear expression. Surprisingly, however, we found that psilocybin did not have replicable effects 24 hours post psilocybin administration on reducing anxiety- and depression-like behaviors or facilitating fear extinction learning. Conclusion: Overall, our comprehensive characterization of psilocybin's acute and persistent behavioral effects using ~200 total male and female mice per experiment spread across five independent labs demonstrates with unique certainty several acute drug effects …

cards.title: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy.
cards.post: Aim: The specific objectives of this systematic review were to: (1) identify extant literature on implementation of PAP, and (2) synthesize and present findings to understand current implementation knowledge and inform future directions. Methods: This systematic review followed the procedures outlined in Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. Results: A total of 2,406 articles were identified, and 2,074 of these were screened by title and abstract after the initial elimination of duplicates and sources that were not peer-reviewed research articles (e.g., gray literature). Forty-seven were retrieved for full text review, and 20 studies were included in the review. Conclusion: There is a noticeable gap in implementation-focused research on best practices for translating PAP from academic settings into accessible clinical programs.

cards.title: Chronic Mild Stress in Male Wistar-Kyoto Rats Induces Long-Term Hippocampal Plasticity Impairments Differentially Reversed by Acute and Chronic Ketamine Treatment.
cards.post: Aim: Here, we investigated how chronic mild stress and subsequent acute and chronic ketamine treatments modulate synaptic plasticity in the Schaffer collateral pathway in the dorsal hippocampus of stress-vulnerable Wistar-Kyoto rats. Methods: Adult male rats were subjected to 4 weeks of chronic mild stress and vulnerability was determined through behavioral performance in the forced swim and elevated plus maze tests. Results: Acute ketamine restored normal LTP but not LTD, while chronic ketamine restored LTD but not LTP. Conclusion: These findings highlight complex temporal dynamics in the modulation of hippocampal synaptic plasticity by ketamine following chronic stress and demonstrate that acute and chronic treatment regimens differentially affect the induction of LTP and LTD.

cards.title: Preclinical Evaluation of [ 18 F]Itareparib, a brain penetrant PARP1-selective radioligand, in Glioma Rat Model and Nonhuman Primate.
cards.venue: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
cards.post: Aim: In this study, we evaluated if [ 18 F]Itareparib, a brain-penetrant, non-trapping, PARP1-selective radioligand with reversible kinetics, could improve brain tumor diagnosis and enable target occupancy studies in neurooncology. Methods: [ 18 F]Itareparib was synthesized and evaluated in an orthotopic rat model of BT142 IDH1-mutant gliomas. Dynamic PET scans were performed with or without the administration of the PARP1-selective inhibitor AZD9574. Results: AZD9574 reduced tumor uptake by 77%, supporting the PARP1-specific binding of [ 18 F]Itareparib in the tumors. In the NHP, [ 18 F]Itareparib showed rapid brain uptake, and V T decreased by 21 ± 6 % after blocking with AZD9574. Conclusion: These findings support further development of [ 18 F]Itareparib for the quantitative PET imaging of PARP1 in brain tumors.

cards.title: Ketamine, an interoceptive associative agent? Evidence from ketamine-assisted Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement for opioid use disorder.
cards.post: Aim: This secondary analysis examined whether ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) added to Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) improved interoceptive awareness and whether these changes mediated reductions in opioid craving. Methods: Sixty-eight adults with OUD receiving buprenorphine were randomized to 8 weeks of MORE with or without KAP. Posttreatment EMA data were available for 18 MORE + KAP and 15 MORE participants. Results: Piecewise modeling showed a greater increase in EMA-assessed body awareness salience in MORE + KAP during days 1–35, spanning the pre-dosing and first-ketamine-dose period ( B = 0.039, standard error (SE) = 0.005, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Adjunctive ketamine was associated with rapid, sustained increases in body awareness salience.

cards.title: Short-term synaptic plasticity modulates the outcome of neurodegenerative diseases.
cards.post: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive neuronal loss and synaptic dysfunction that disrupt memory-encoding neural circuits. Methods: Using the NEST Simulator, a spiking neural network of 1,000 Hodgkin-Huxley excitatory neurons and 250 leaky integrate-and-fire inhibitory neurons was constructed with embedded memory engram assemblies. Results: Increasing τfac from 500 ms to 1,250ms rescued engram selectivity in the AD model at intermediate synaptic-weight regimes that were inaccessible at baseline, and partially restored theta-band LFP power while fully restoring alpha-band LFP power. Conclusion: Short-term synaptic facilitation (STF) and short-term synaptic depression (STD) modulation exert mechanistically distinct compensatory effects.

cards.title: 18F-Labeled 7-Azaindole-Based Radioligands for Imaging Colony-Stimulating Factor 1 Receptor in Glioblastoma
cards.post: Background: A series of 7-azaindole-based compounds were designed and synthesized as novel colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor (CSF1R) ligands. Methods: Among them, [18F]PLX6 (IC50 = 12.3 nM) showed modest brain uptake and rapid clearance in rats. Micro-PET/CT imaging resulted in clear visualization of both subcutaneous and intracranial orthotopic U87MG gliomas. Results: Treatment with PLX3397 or PLX5622 significantly reduced tumor uptake, indicating specific binding of [18F]PLX6 to CSF1R. Ex vivo autoradiography at 30 min postinjection (p.i.) confirmed high tumor-to-brain ratio (10.14 ± 1.52) and specific binding of [18F]PLX6 to CSF1R. Conclusion: These results support further evaluation of [18F]PLX6 as a promising PET imaging agent for noninvasive visualization of CSF1R expression in glioblastoma.

cards.title: Mechanism-guided generative chemistry yields distinct agonist-like and antagonist-like ligand populations for the serotonin 5-HT2A receptor
cards.post: Background: Designing serotonin 5-HT2A receptor ligands with a specified functional direction is difficult because binding affinity, assay-derived mechanism labels, molecular properties and receptor conformation are only partially coupled. Methods: We developed a mechanism-guided generative chemistry workflow integrating curated ChEMBL data, scaffold-aware supervised learning, a recurrent SMILES prior, reinforcement learning, medicinal-chemistry prioritization, receptor-context docking, MM-GBSA rescoring and property-adjusted contact analysis. Results: Antagonist-like candidates showed higher predicted affinity and mechanism-label confidence, whereas agonist-like candidates showed higher QED, greater internal diversity and lower training-set similarity. Conclusion: The study identifies distinct model-defined chemical regimes and links campaign-level property drift to receptor-contact topology; generated compounds remain computational hypotheses requiring experimental validation.

cards.title: Personalized Prediction of Differences in fMRI Connectivity Estimates Across Preprocessing Pipelines
cards.post: Background: Longitudinal functional MRI of the human brain is valuable for tracking changes in functional connectivity (FC) associated with disease progression or treatment response. Methods: Even so, measured FC values depend on preprocessing, and nuisance regression and temporal filtering affect individuals differently. We examined whether we could use earlier scans to predict how preprocessing would affect a later scan. Results: This advantage persisted after accounting for acquisition variables. The ADNI-trained model reduced mean error in ten Midnight Scan Club participants without refitting. Conclusion: These results support using personal preprocessing history to predict changes in connectivity estimates on newly acquired scans.

cards.title: Counteracting the overestimation of effect size in mass-univariate brain-wide association studies using cross-validation.
cards.post: Background: Brain-wide association effects are commonly overestimated in psychiatric neuroimaging research, leading to low replicability and generalizability of findings, and ultimately to poor translation to clinical utility. Methods: We systematically evaluated the benefit of a cross-validation procedure to expose inflated effect size estimates in mass-univariate voxel-based analysis, using body mass index (BMI) as an example predictor for gray matter. Results: BMI was negatively associated with gray matter density with a maximum underlying effect size of R² p = 0.036 (in the full sample of n = 3401). Even with an underlying null-effect, effect size estimates up to R² p = 0.429 were reached in samples with n = 25. Conclusion: Results suggest that cross-validation is an effective measure to expose overestimated effects in small samples and thus could help to counteract low replicability and generalizability in brain-wide mass-univariate association studies.

cards.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
cards.post: Aim: To assess whether resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity differs between high-intelligence individuals (MENSA members) and controls using graph-theory metrics: clustering coefficient, characteristic path length, and small-worldness. Methods: Resting-state 64-channel EEG data were recorded in 29 MENSA participants and 20 controls. Functional connectivity was estimated using Lagged Linear Coherence across delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands. Results: Compared with controls, MENSA participants showed significantly lower characteristic path length in the alpha band (Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) critical value = 0.004), indicating greater global network integration. Conclusion: These findings support a nuanced neural-efficiency model of intelligence without changes in small-world architecture.

cards.title: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago.
cards.post: Background: Cannabis is the world's most-used illicit psychoactive plant, yet direct prehistoric evidence for its consumption is rare. Methods: In this study, we present the earliest direct evidence of cannabis use: offerings of plant parts and chemical compounds in ancient human hair recovered from a monumental tomb in Siberia. Conclusion: The findings suggest that the plant was used for its psychoactive qualities across Eurasia, where specific wild populations might have had naturally higher active compound levels.

cards.title: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children's everyday speech.
cards.post: Background: Children learn to understand and speak from the speech around them, yet how that everyday input shapes learning remains unresolved. Methods: We trained cognitively feasible, child-specific models on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1000 days of life. Conclusion: These findings show that everyday experience contains sufficient structure for language learning and establish child-specific modeling for testing developmental theories.

cards.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes.
cards.post: Aim: Here we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type-specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behaviour generation and learning. Methods: We record longitudinally while animals train through direct aggression experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behaviour and neural activity in a novel aggression context. Results: During aggression observation, observed behaviour recruits widespread activation across subcortical networks for behavioural generation and mimics activity evoked by experienced behaviour, and shared neural changes persist into the novel aggression context. Conclusion: Together, this demonstrates that experience-like activity during aggression observation can recruit a shared inhibitory plasticity mechanism that biases behaviour toward adaptive proactive behavioural strategies.

cards.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity.
cards.post: Aim: Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography12 due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Methods: Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. Results: The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers13. The large area of Laurentia and limited deformation at its margins explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved and documented there. Conclusion: Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents1,14, and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

cards.title: Subacute effects of the psychedelic ayahuasca on the salience and default mode networks
cards.post: Aim: This study explores the subacute changes of primary sensory brain networks and networks supporting higher-order affective and self-referential functions 24 hours after a single session with the psychedelic ayahuasca. Methods: We leveraged task-free functional magnetic resonance imaging data 1 day before and 1 day after a randomized placebo-controlled trial exploring the effects of ayahuasca in naïve healthy participants (21 placebo/22 ayahuasca). Results: Our findings revealed increased anterior cingulate cortex connectivity within the salience network, decreased posterior cingulate cortex connectivity within the default mode network, and increased connectivity between the salience and default mode networks 1 day after the session in the ayahuasca group compared to placebo. Conclusion: These findings provide preliminary evidence for subacute functional changes induced by the psychedelic ayahuasca on higher-order cognitive brain networks that support interoceptive, affective, and self-referential functions.

cards.title: Default Mode Network Modulation by Psychedelics: A Systematic Review
cards.post: Background: Psychedelics are a unique class of drug that commonly produce vivid hallucinations as well as profound psychological and mystical experiences. Methods: To date, several studies have investigated how psychedelics modulate this network, but no comprehensive review, to our knowledge, has critically evaluated how major classical psychedelic agents-lysergic acid diethylamide, psilocybin, and ayahuasca-modulate the DMN. Results: Across psychedelics there is consistent acute disruption in resting state connectivity within the DMN and increased functional connectivity between canonical resting-state networks. Various models have been proposed to explain the cognitive mechanisms of psychedelics, and in one model DMN modulation is a central axiom. Conclusion: This article aims to provide the field with a comprehensive overview that can propel future research in such a way as to elucidate the neurocognitive mechanisms of psychedelics.
